description.zh: 京都拥有超过1,600座寺庙和400座神社，其中金阁寺、清水寺、岚山竹林等最为著名。17处被列入UNESCO世界遗产，每年春季赏樱和秋季赏枫时节吸引数以百万计的游客。
description.en: Kyoto has over 1,600 temples and 400 shrines, with 17 UNESCO-listed structures including Kinkaku-ji, Kiyomizu-dera and Ryoan-ji. Cherry blossom and autumn foliage seasons draw millions.

zh: 17处UNESCO遗产建筑，含金阁寺、龙安寺、二条城
四季主题：春樱、夏绿、秋枫、冬雪
金阁寺、清水寺、岚山竹林各具特色
en: 17 UNESCO-listed structures including Kinkaku-ji, Ryoan-ji and Nijo Castle
Seasonal beauty: cherry blossoms, green summer, autumn foliage, winter snow
Kinkaku-ji, Kiyomizu-dera and Arashiyama each unmissable

admission.zh: 各寺庙单独收费，一般500—1,000日元

tips.zh: 花见（3月底—4月初）和红叶（11月中）期间人极多，住宿需提前3个月预订。
tips.en: Cherry blossom (late March–early April) and autumn foliage (mid-November) bring enormous crowds; book accommodation 3 months ahead.

description.zh: 伏见稻荷大社是全日本约30,000座稻荷神社的总本社，供奉五谷丰收与商业繁荣之神。以从本殿绵延至稻荷山山顶的「千本鸟居」（实际超过10,000座朱红色鸟居）举世闻名，全程约4公里登山路线穿越连续的鸟居隧道，自古是京都香火最旺的参拜地之一。
description.en: Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of Japan's ~30,000 Inari shrines, dedicated to the gods of rice harvest and business prosperity. It is world-famous for its 'senbon torii' (literally 'thousand torii gates' — actually over 10,000 vermilion gates) lining the 4 km mountain trail to the summit of Mt Inari. One of Kyoto's most-visited shrines since ancient times.

location.zh: 京都府京都市伏见区深草薮之内町

zh: 千本鸟居：超过10,000座朱红色鸟居连绵排列，形成令人叹为观止的隧道景观
稻荷山登山：全程约4公里，途经奥社、三ノ峰等多处参拜所，山顶海拔233米
狐狸信仰：稻荷神的使者为狐狸，神社内遍布以狐狸为主题的装饰、御守和石雕
en: Senbon torii: 10,000+ vermilion torii forming awe-inspiring tunnel corridors up the mountain
Mt Inari hike: ~4 km full circuit past Okusho and Sannomiya shrines to the 233 m summit
Fox iconography: foxes are the messengers of the Inari deity — fox sculptures, amulets and decorations fill the grounds

duration.en: 1.5–3 hours depending on how far you hike

tips.zh: 清晨5—7点人流极少，是拍摄朱红鸟居最佳时机。从JR京都站乘奈良线约5分钟至稻荷站，直达神社正门。日落后至深夜亦别有意境，神社有夜间照明。
tips.en: 5–7 am offers near-empty torii corridors — the best window for photography. Take the JR Nara Line 5 minutes from Kyoto Station to Inari station, stepping out directly at the main gate. The shrine is also beautifully lit after dark.
